subject: Coordinating multi-year conversion: co-term bridging + ramp cadence
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@velocityhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Coordinating multi-year conversion: co-term bridging + ramp cadence

Samir —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together a pragmatic path to convert Velocity Health from an annual reserve to a multi-year committed model while keeping your billing and renewal boundary aligned to your fiscal July window. High level:

- 24-month commitment with a staged ramp (Year 1 = 60% of committed tokens, Year 2 = 100%); this protects you from front-loaded spend while giving Redwood predictability for capacity.
- Co-terming: we propose a short bridge period (4 months) to align existing contracts, then full co-term on July 1, 2026.
- Auto-renew: default auto-renew with a 60-day opt-out window; we can add a manual review trigger at $X usage variance if you prefer.

Attached: redwood_term_sheet_v2.pdf (term summary) and a sample velocity_capacity_ramp.xlsx that maps how capacity converts to committed buckets across months.

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether Velocity wants an explicit auto-renew opt-out or a manual review clause?
2) If legal wants specific language, loop them to this thread and we’ll fast-track the redlines.
3) Proposed internal kickoff: Sep 16 — we’ll provision a staging pool and schedule a run-rate review in 30 days.

I’ll be out Tuesday morning but reachable on Slack.

Best,
Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_term_sheet_v2.pdf (summary page), velocity_capacity_ramp.xlsx

From: Samir Patel <samir@velocityhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Coordinating multi-year conversion: co-term bridging + ramp cadence

Thanks Camila — appreciate the clear plan. A few quick clarifying items from our side:

1) Pricing delta: can you confirm the per-token uplift if we go to a 24-month vs 12-month term? Finance will need a line item.
2) Ramp guarantee: if our usage accelerates faster than the Year 1 ramp, do we get immediate access to higher-capacity pools or is there a provisioning lead?
3) Auto-renew: legal prefers "manual renewal unless both parties agree to auto-renew" but understands commercial teams prefer automatic renewal for continuity. Can you propose compromise language?

Looping in Velocity Health Legal on cc for redline transparency. Also: we prefer DocuSign for the final term sheet.

- Samir
VP Product, Velocity Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 13:08:10 -0700
Subject: RE: Coordinating multi-year conversion: co-term bridging + ramp cadence

Quick internal note and suggested language for Samir / legal:

Pricing delta: recommend we present two pricing options clearly (A = 24m: 13% unit discount vs current; B = 12m: 8% unit discount). Call it out as a blended-per-token for clarity. I attached a short worksheet to the Drive folder (see related_links).

Ramp & provisioning: operationally we can guarantee immediate access to extra capacity up to a 20% burst buffer (no additional provisioning lead) for the first 90 days after signing. Anything beyond that we handle via a 5-business-day provisioning SLA. This gives Velocity runway while protecting planned pools.

Auto-renew compromise wording (proposal): "This Agreement will automatically renew for successive one (1) year terms unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may opt-out of automatic renewal for any renewal term by providing written notice within forty-five (45) days after execution of this Agreement, after which the Agreement will not auto-renew for the subsequent term."

Co-term bridging mechanics: 4-month short bridge where Redwood credits pro-rata unused portion of the current year into the Year 1 commitment to avoid double-billing.

I think this is defensible and clean for legal. If Samir wants we can push to DocuSign today once he confirms the opt-out preference.

-Karthik
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@velocityhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Velocity Health Legal <legal@velocityhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Coordinating multi-year conversion: co-term bridging + ramp cadence

Samir —

Thanks — this is great context. Answering your items inline: 

1) Pricing: see two options below (blended per-token) — happy to run a quick spreadsheet walk-through.
   - Option A (24m): 13% discount vs current list = $0.065 / token (blended)
   - Option B (12m): 8% discount vs current list = $0.071 / token (blended)

2) Ramp/provisioning: we will provide a 20% burst buffer for 90 days and then a 5-business-day provisioning SLA for increases beyond that.

3) Auto-renew: Karthik proposed compromise language above. If Velocity Legal can accept that, we will produce a final term sheet and send via DocuSign link (attached in related_links).

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Velocity to confirm auto-renew preference (accept compromise language or propose edits) — target: Sep 12.
- On confirmation we will prepare the DocuSign packet and include a short SOW for the staging pool.
- Sep 16 internal kickoff remains on the table pending sign.

If Legal wants a redline, we can accept up to minor clarifications on notice windows without altering economics.

Thanks again — I’ll stand by for confirmation and will queue the DocuSign packet once we have the opt-out direction.

Best,
Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
